commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Wangsa
Add Wangsa greeting and exit flow
Add command echo and bye exit
Add task storage and list command
Add task status commands and Task class
Add todo deadline and event tasks

commitResults.messageBody: Introduce a portable text format that preserves task types, details, and completion state. Validate saved records before loading so damaged data cannot silently replace the active task list.
Load persisted tasks during startup and save after every successful list mutation. Stop safely on storage errors so the in-memory list is never presented as durable when writing fails.
Parse deadline input as LocalDate so invalid calendar dates are rejected early. Persist dates in stable ISO form while displaying a clearer English month format to users.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-8: use structured deadline dates

commitResults.messageBody: Introduce TaskList as the owner of ordering, capacity, validation, and mutations. Adapt Storage and Wangsa to exchange collection snapshots instead of coordinating a raw array and count.
Move command recognition, argument validation, task construction, and deadline date parsing into Parser. Wangsa now dispatches typed command categories without owning input syntax.
Reject unsupported task text inside Parser and handle ADD_TASK explicitly in Wangsa. This prevents future command types from being misinterpreted as event creation.
Move input, output, message formatting, and scanner lifecycle into Ui. Reshape Wangsa into a testable coordinator with a run method and injected Parser, TaskList, Storage, and UI collaborators.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize application classes in duke package
commitResults.messageBody: Place the complete application under the duke package while keeping src/main/java as the source root. Update the setup guide to launch duke.Wangsa so the packaged entry point remains discoverable.
Complete the A-Packages move by deleting the obsolete default-package copies, leaving src/main/java/duke as the single source location.
Add a reproducible Gradle 9.1.0 wrapper, Java 25 toolchain configuration, and the application run task for duke.Wangsa. Forward standard input so the chatbot remains interactive under Gradle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit coverage for core behavior
commitResults.messageBody: Configure Gradle to run JUnit Jupiter tests and cover TaskList mutations, Parser command/date handling, and Storage round-tripping and corruption cases.
Complete Javadoc for constructors, accessors, collection operations, and UI methods so generated documentation is warning-free.
Capture the SE-EDU Java and Git conventions as reusable project guidance so future source changes and commit messages follow the same rules.
Require the reusable Java and Git standard skills for future work while preserving the existing project guidance and student profile.

Users need a way to locate tasks without scanning the full list. Add case-insensitive description search, validate the find keyword, display matching tasks, and cover matching and empty-result behavior with JUnit tests.

Distribute the application as build/libs/Wangsa.jar with a duke.Wangsa
entry point and document the build and run commands. Clean up the new
Level-9 Javadocs to match the project coding standard.
